Worlds and evidence

A world is the complete case behind a question: its records, documents, changes over time, and reference answer. Think of it as one folder of material prepared for one investigation. A model sees the allowed documents from that folder.

Keeping the world fixed lets us repeat a question with another model or change one condition—such as adding irrelevant documents—and measure the effect.

Three ways to build a world

1. Use Open Targets records

Open Targets worlds select relationships from a pinned database release. A case can include a drug acting on a target and that target being associated with a disease. The question asks the model to connect the supplied records.

For example, LEVOBUPIVACAINE → SCN4A → pharyngitis connects a target action with a disease association. Relationship types and action attributes, such as agonism or antagonism, retain their meaning. This route does not establish that the drug treats the disease.

Use this kind of world to test reasoning over real database records. The answer is about the supplied records, rather than every fact that might exist elsewhere.

2. Turn the records into a document corpus

The same kind of information can be presented as a source review, a laboratory note or an email. The model must find the relevant sentences, follow citations, and distinguish an observation from an untested proposal.

For example, one document might state the drug–target relationship, while another reports the target–disease association. A third may repeat a tentative idea as though it were established. The task now tests reading and source assessment as well as joining relationships.

These are authored benchmark documents based on a supplied plan. They are not original published papers. Each actual source record still needs its identity and qualifications.

3. Create controlled fictional facts

A controlled world can assign a fresh value to an entity—for example, “Aster's registry category is cobalt”—and later replace it with “amber.” The model cannot obtain that new assignment from background knowledge. It has to use this episode's evidence.

Use this kind of world to isolate recall, updates or following a chain of records. Its fresh assignments are deliberately fictional, even if familiar entity names are used.

How a record becomes a sentence the model reads

Consider this simple statement: Drug A acts on Target B. The factual plan keeps several pieces of information that serve different purposes:

ConceptMeaningExample
SubjectThe entity the statement starts fromDrug A
RelationHow it is connected to another entityacts on
ObjectThe entity at the other endTarget B
AttributesExtra detail about that connectionaction type: inhibitor
ProvenanceWhere the record came fromdatabase release and record ID
Public assertionThe sentence the document is meant to express“Drug A inhibits Target B”
MentionOne occurrence of that assertionThe sentence in document D02
PassageIts exact location in the final textCharacters 120–157 in D02

The plan is represented in code by FactPlan. Readers do not need to construct that object manually; it keeps the generation and scoring stages aligned.

A mention also records how the sentence should be read:

  • Status: is it clinical evidence, genetic evidence, literature, or a hypothesis?
  • Polarity: does it support the relationship or argue against it?
  • Hedge: is it stated confidently, tentatively, or with substantial uncertainty?
  • Source relationship: is it independent evidence or a repetition of another source?
  • Retraction: has a later notice withdrawn this particular earlier statement?
  • Planned corruption: was the public sentence intentionally made misleading for a test?

A document plan supplies a purpose, genre, date and author/laboratory wrapper. Those wrappers help make the text readable; they do not turn repeated information into a new independent scientific source.

A source is not the same as a document

Two documents can repeat one study. That gives the model two places to find the claim, but only one underlying source. A section is simply part of a document. Splitting a long document into five sections does not create five independent observations.

This matters when the question needs corroboration or when a claim has been withdrawn. The runner and scorer must track the source that supports a claim, rather than simply count how many times its wording appears.

Respondent inputs and evaluator references

Model receivesEvaluator keeps separately
The question and rules for using evidenceThe expected answer and how it was derived
The supplied documents and visible source detailsWhich statements are relevant or deliberately problematic
Dates, stated uncertainty and withdrawal noticesThe intended corruption and its target passage
Any glossary explaining aliasesThe private mapping used to change entity names

The model must be able to work out the answer from the left column. Information in the right column is for checking its work afterward. A review page may reveal both, so it must not be used as the model's input.

Explore an actual extracted neighborhood

Explore the LEVOBUPIVACAINE → SCN4A → pharyngitis neighborhood and a bounded set of recorded neighbors. Select an entity, filter relationships or inspect an exact edge. The view preserves the distinction between target actions, disease associations and clinical indications.

Open this page in the documentation reader with JavaScript enabled to explore the frozen data. No model calls or benchmark evaluation are started by these controls.
